def: Training in which every rank must finish each step's communication before any rank continues, so one failed or slow rank stops or slows the whole job.
A snapshot of all state needed to resume training exactly: weights, optimiser state, step, data position and random-number states.
The share of elapsed wall-clock time spent on useful training, after subtracting restarts, lost work and checkpoint pauses.
A working but slow GPU, host or link that sets the pace of a synchronous job because everyone waits for it.
A hardware fault that makes a computation return a wrong value without raising any error.
A failure in which no rank crashes but progress stops, typically because one rank never joins a collective operation.
The checkpoint interval that minimises wasted time, approximately the square root of twice the checkpoint cost times the mean time between failures.
Copying training state to host memory quickly and writing it to storage in the background, so GPUs pause only for the copy.
A checkpoint in which each rank writes only the part of the state it owns, in parallel, rather than gathering everything to one writer.
A sudden jump in training loss, often preceded by a gradient-norm burst, that may or may not recover without rolling back to an earlier checkpoint.
A ring buffer of recent communication events and stack traces per rank, dumped when a watchdog fires so a hang can be traced to its cause.
